title: Design System: Murilo Neves Teixeira · portfólio

display-hero.purpose: The hero name and the contact title only.

headline.purpose: Project titles and the timeline heading.

title.purpose: Row names in the oneline list and stat table; the nav wordmark.

lede.purpose: The hero message and the contact lede.

body.purpose: Running copy; 1.1rem for project descriptions and about paragraphs.

mono-label.purpose: Hashes, command sublines, meta, stack lines, nav links, terminal output, dates.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Screenshot plates, phone inset, terminal and cursor preview: objects lifted off the printout.

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: Filled buttons on hover, with a 2px rise.

shadows.name: head-halo
shadows.purpose: Yolk halo around the HEAD dot in the nav readout.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single easing for every transition and entrance.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover, color, sweep and wipe changes.

motion.name: entrance
motion.purpose: Hero name rise, hero stack fade-up, plate unroll (clip-path), node scale-in.

motion.name: stat-type
motion.purpose: Stagger of the + characters in the stat bars.

motion.name: ambient
motion.value: caret blink 1.05s steps(1); HEAD ring 2.4s; status pulse 2s; mascot hop 1.4s
motion.purpose: The only looping motion; all collapse under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
The whole site is one `git log --graph` that prints itself as you scroll. A thick, ink-cased rail runs down a fixed left gutter; the HEAD marker (a yolk node with a `HEAD` tag) rides it with the scroll position; each featured project forks off `main` on its own colored lane, collects its feature list as commits, and merges back with a literal `Merge branch 'feat/…' into main` line. The hero is a live canvas graph the visitor can grow by moving and clicking. Programming is the material, not a costume: hashes are real commits, the nav carries a typed shell prompt and a `HEAD → <section>` readout, and the about section holds a working terminal.

The world sits on a deep cobalt floor (never black), printed in chalk and ink, and lit by six saturated lane colors borrowed from the graph. Three sections leave the cobalt and become full-bleed bands of paper, yolk and ember, so the scroll reads as a printout changing stock. Type is a two-voice system: Bricolage Grotesque condensed to 75% width at weight 800 shouts names and headings, and Martian Mono reports everything the machine would print (hashes, refs, commands, counts, dates). Density is generous: big section padding, long single columns of log lines, one project per screen-and-a-half.

The direction contract explicitly refuses the "black terminal + glowing cards" portfolio. The build honors that: terminals exist, but as ink objects sitting on cobalt, and there are no glows, glass cards or gradient fills anywhere outside the hero's legibility veil.
keyCharacteristics: Cobalt ground with an ink-cased commit rail in a fixed left gutter on every section.
One lane color per project branch, carried by every lane-colored element of that project.
Full-bleed paper, yolk and ember bands as section grounds.
Condensed 800-weight Bricolage display against Martian Mono machine output.
Pills for every ref, button, nav link and chip; generously rounded plates for screenshots.
Motion that prints: nodes scale in, log lines light up as HEAD passes, plates unroll top-down, `+` bars type out.

rules.name: The Cobalt Floor Rule
rules.body: The page ground is cobalt (#141d8a), never black or near-black. Ink (#0a0f3d) is for objects placed on the floor (terminal, config, footer, casings), never for the floor itself.

rules.name: The One Lane, One Color Rule
rules.body: Each project branch sets a single `--lane` color, and every lane-colored element of that project (its rail, its commit nodes, its ref pill, its `+` marks, its screenshot plate, its primary button, its merge line) uses it. Text on a lane fill is always ink.

rules.name: The Yolk Is HEAD Rule
rules.body: Yolk marks the current position and the main action: HEAD, primary button, focus, selection, caret. Do not spend it on decoration.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Band Rule
rules.body: Paper, yolk and ember appear as whole section grounds edge to edge, flat. They are never gradients, tinted cards or partial panels. On those bands, text is ink and accent text drops to its deep variant.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Bricolage speaks (names, headings, prose, buttons); Martian Mono reports (anything git or a shell would print: hashes, refs, commands, counts, dates, URLs, config keys). Never set a prose sentence in mono, and never set a hash or ref in Bricolage.

rules.name: The Condensed Shout Rule
rules.body: Every heading from Title up is weight 800 at 75–80% width with negative tracking and line-height under 1.1. Headings are never light, never wide, never letter-spaced open.

rules.name: The Command Subline Rule
rules.body: A section heading is followed (never preceded) by the mono git command that would produce it, with a dimmer plain-language gloss after a middle dot: `git diff --stat · quantos dos meus 16 repositórios públicos usam cada coisa`.

rules.name: The Rail Gutter Rule
rules.body: Nothing but the graph lives in the left gutter. Every section, band and footer indents its content by the gutter so the rail never collides with copy.

rules.name: The Breakpoint Ladder Rule
rules.body: The system's breakpoints are 1100px (fold wide tables, drop the nav prompt), 960px (single-column projects and about), 760px (compact gutter and nav, mobile hero) and 360px (tightest nav links). New surfaces fold at the same steps.

rules.name: The Flat Printout Rule
rules.body: Sections, bands, list rows and panels inside the flow are flat. A shadow means "this object sits on top of the page", and only plates, the terminal, the preview and buttons qualify.

dos: **Do** keep the page on Cobalt Ground (#141d8a) and switch section grounds only to full-bleed Paper, Yolk or Ember bands.
**Do** give every new project exactly one lane color from the six-color set (ember, yolk, mint, pink, sky, lilac) and route it through `--lane` to its rail, nodes, ref, `+` marks, plate and button.
**Do** set ink (#0a0f3d) text on every yolk, ember, paper, mint and lane-colored fill.
**Do** indent all content by the gutter (128px, 46px at 760px and below) so the commit rail stays clear.
**Do** follow every section heading with its mono git command subline, and put hashes and refs in Martian Mono at 87.5% width.
**Do** use the single easing `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and make every reveal print, light up or unroll; provide a reduced-motion path that shows the final state.
**Do** keep mono labels at 0.7rem or larger.
donts: **Don't** put the page on black or near-black, or build "black terminal + glowing cards"; the direction contract refuses it.
**Don't** add glows, neon text-shadows, glassmorphism or gradient fills; the only gradient in the system is the hero's legibility veil.
**Don't** give a project two lane colors, or use a lane color outside its own project article.
**Don't** spend yolk on decoration; it means HEAD, primary action and focus.
**Don't** put shadows on bands, list rows or in-flow panels; only plates, the terminal, the preview and buttons float.
**Don't** set prose in mono or hashes and refs in Bricolage.
**Don't** set light-band accent text in the bright accent; use the deep variant (ember-deep on paper, mint-deep or yolk-umber on yolk).
**Don't** place anything but the graph in the left gutter.
